feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{2}{3})=-0.729\,727…≈-0.7297\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-0.729\,7$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-0.7297.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=0.7297.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.7297.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/92b256db68d09a07e5072d12cb18470e2c165b6f3c8aa29c6953d9aebb3b024e.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +0.7297 \\  & ≈3.8713\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get the second solution ${x}_{2}$ that's within the given domain, we simply subtract $2\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=X-2\pi  & =3.871\,3-2\pi ≈-2.4119\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈-2.4,\,x≈-0.7.
$$
